title: Judge the feedback apart from the verdict
statement: Check a marker's feedback text on its own, apart from its verdicts: every verdict can be right while the feedback misreads the text or the student's answer.
example: In one probe all 16 verdicts were right, and 2 replies misread the text or the child's answer.
detail: A live probe sent 16 answers to a reading engine's marker on four open items: all 16 verdicts were right, with no held pass and no passed hold, but two replies misread, one steering the child toward the wrong trigger for a character's habit and one crediting a story detail the child had never mentioned (`grade3-reading/artifacts/peter-pan-standing-2026-09-11/readiness-l5-2026-09-17/sim-review/lens-judge-probe.md`). The probe classed both as failures of the feedback text, not of the scoring, so a test of verdicts alone would have passed them; an earlier run of the same inputs had given correct replies.
against: The probe was an AI review's: its expected verdicts were set by agents, not labelled by a person (`grade3-reading/artifacts/peter-pan-standing-2026-09-11/readiness-l5-2026-09-17/sim-review/LENSES-RESULT.md`).

evidence.quote: All 16 bands are correct. No held pass and no passed hold found. Two coaching-text issues found on p19, both in the `swyk-dialogue` node.
These findings are coaching-text quality failures, not scoring failures.
